issues.source_quote: Те сидят там, в Средней Азии, а этот под Москвой.
issues.translation_quote: Those two are inside out in Central Asia, he's near Moscow.
issues.justification: 'inside out' is a garbled rendering of 'сидят' (are serving time); also 'two' vs. original plural and 'near Moscow' lacks 'inside'. Meaning is distorted and confusing.

issues.source_quote: Нехороший человек? - Редиска.
issues.translation_quote: A bad person? - A radish.
issues.justification: The thieves' slang 'редиска' (a lowlife/bad guy) becomes a running gag; rendering as 'radish' with no explanation makes it opaque, and later 'not-nice person' glosses are inconsistent with 'bad person'. The joke of the slang lesson partly fails.

issues.source_quote: Хороший человек? Забыл! Фрей-фея, действительно: Фрей-фея.
issues.translation_quote: A good person? Forgot! A mark... right, a mark.
issues.justification: 'Фраер' is mistranslated as 'mark'; also the humor of the character's slip (фрей-фея) is lost. The original word is a thieves' term for a sucker/straight person; 'mark' is a different notion and the phonetic wordplay is gone.

issues.source_quote: Ес, ес, ОБХС.
issues.translation_quote: Yes, yes, IRS.
issues.justification: ОБХС (Soviet anti-embezzlement police) is replaced by the American IRS, an anachronistic and inaccurate substitution that breaks the Soviet setting; the joke (thieves hearing 'yes, yes' as the police unit) is lost.

issues.source_quote: Скажите, сколько весит этот шлем? ... Тяжелая шапочка.
issues.translation_quote: Heavy little hat.
issues.justification: Fine, but the jocular tone is partially kept. (Not flagged.)

issues.source_quote: Нас четверо. - И все заведующие? Вроде.
issues.translation_quote: - And all of you heads? - Sort of.
issues.justification: 'Вроде' here is a deadpan, slightly evasive answer; acceptable. However 'Заведую 83-м детсадом' is rendered 'I run Kindergarten No. 83', fine. (Not an issue.)

issues.source_quote: Это у нас с ними цацкаются, на поруки берут
issues.translation_quote: Here we coddle them, release them on probation
issues.justification: 'На поруки' means release on a collective's surety, not probation; a Soviet-specific concept flattened.

issues.source_quote: Эй, гражданина! Ты туда не ходи, ты сюда ходи, а то снег башка попадет - совсем мертвый будешь!
issues.translation_quote: Hey, citizen-man! You no go there, you go here, or snow hit head - you be all dead!
issues.justification: Parody of a broken-Russian Central Asian accent works, but elsewhere the same pidgin is applied inconsistently to Vasya (e.g., 'Give tenner, I buy kerosene stove') while at times he speaks normally ('Shakal I parshivy' rendered as 'I'm mangy jackal'); pidgin is overused and makes characters sound cartoonish in places where the Russian is merely colloquial (e.g., 'Why you so mean? Why like a dog?' for Vasya).

issues.source_quote: Мы будем прятать, а он дырка смотреть?
issues.translation_quote: We hide, and he look through hole?
issues.justification: Russian is Vasya's broken speech but rendering as pidgin is acceptable; however the line 'Зачем? Давай ты выйдешь' reply attribution confusion is not relevant. Minor inconsistency in Vasya's voice across scenes.

issues.source_quote: Тики так! ... Тики-так.
issues.translation_quote: Tickety-boo!
issues.justification: 'Тики-так' is thieves' slang for 'okay/all right'; 'tickety-boo' is a British upper-class idiom, creating a register and era mismatch for Soviet criminals.

issues.source_quote: Пивная? - Тошниловка.
issues.translation_quote: Beer hall? - Pukeateria.
issues.justification: 'Pukeateria' is a forced, cutesy coinage unlike the gritty slang of the original (тошниловка = greasy spoon dive); register mismatch.

issues.source_quote: Вы Ваши 20 рублей положите в эту тумбочку, а на двери замок повесьте.
issues.translation_quote: Put your 20 rubles in this nightstand, and hang a lock on the door.
issues.justification: The scheme (they lock the room so the 'pay' stays and they collect later) is rendered adequately, but 'Замок будет крепкий' loses menace. Minor; but 'Cut the chatter' etc fine.

issues.source_quote: Против бритвы - пиджак и брюки. Только пиджак.
issues.translation_quote: Jacket and trousers against the razor. - Just the jacket.
issues.justification: Chess-play context and stakes are muddled; 'Ходи лошадью' (move the knight) rendered as 'Move the horse' which is non-idiomatic for chess in English.

issues.source_quote: Ходи лошадью, лошадью ходи, дурак!
issues.translation_quote: Move the horse, move the horse, you fool!
issues.justification: In English chess the piece is 'knight'; 'horse' is a literal rendering. Even if a layman's slang, it reads odd.

issues.source_quote: Это не смешно, тетя. - Не смешно. За мной.
issues.translation_quote: - That's not funny, auntie. - Not funny. Follow me.
issues.justification: 'Auntie' for a Russian 'тетя' addressed to a woman is acceptable, but the preceding 'Вор он.' joke is fine. Minor.

issues.source_quote: Он, говорят, Рябого бритвой по горлу - чик и приветик.
issues.translation_quote: They say he did Ryaboy with a razor across the throat - snick, and bye-bye.
issues.justification: Acceptable. (Not an issue.)

issues.source_quote: Носи на здоровье, домашние.
issues.translation_quote: Wear them in good health, house slippers.
issues.justification: 'Домашние' are house slippers; fine. But the following 'А пока и в тюрьме пригодятся' ok.

issues.source_quote: Физкультпривет!
issues.translation_quote: Fitness greetings!
issues.justification: A Soviet-era jocular greeting ('physical-culture hello') is rendered stiffly; the comic effect is weak and it is repeated mechanically.

issues.source_quote: Кому говорят? ... Навуходоносор, - петух гамбургский!
issues.translation_quote: you wiener, you sausage, you radish, you Nebuchadnezzar, - you Hamburg rooster!
issues.justification: Comic insults are kept, but 'сарделька, сосиска' are rendered as 'wiener, sausage' ok. Acceptable.

issues.source_quote: Какая зараза хмыренку этому на Хмыря накапала?
issues.translation_quote: What rat squealed on Khmyr to that little Khmyr?
issues.justification: Confusing: 'хмыренок' is Khmyr's son (Khmyr's kid); the translation loses that the kid is the son. Also 'Hanged himself' earlier 'Хмырь повесился' is a mistranslation of the scene (he is faking a suicide / was hanging himself attempt).

issues.source_quote: Хмырь повесился.
issues.translation_quote: Khmyr's hanged himself.
issues.justification: Fine. (Not an issue.)

issues.source_quote: Сколько я зарезал, сколько перерезал, сколько душ я загубил!
issues.translation_quote: So many I've knifed, so many I've sliced, so many souls I've sent to their graves!
issues.justification: This line is a deliberate parody of a famous Russian folk-song/'robber' refrain and the persona 'Никола Питерский'; the translation keeps the content but loses the rhythmic parody.

issues.source_quote: Ты, Федя, ... Теперь, Федя, скажи Васе все, что ты ему сказал, на гражданском языке.
issues.translation_quote: in civilian language
issues.justification: 'Civilian language' is an awkward calque; 'plain language' would be more natural.

issues.source_quote: Не хотелось Вам говорить
issues.translation_quote: I didn't want to tell you
issues.justification: Fine.

issues.source_quote: Чегой-то ты воруешь?
issues.translation_quote: What're you stealing?
issues.justification: Loses the folksy rustic marker, minor.

issues.source_quote: Нам не страшен серый волк
issues.translation_quote: Who's afraid of the big bad wolf
issues.justification: Replaces the Soviet song with the Disney song; changes cultural reference and the following parody ('Я злой и страшный серый волк') is rendered as invented rhymes that drift from the source.

issues.source_quote: Шах! ... Мат!
issues.translation_quote: Check! ... Mate!
issues.justification: Fine. (Not an issue.)

issues.source_quote: Те сидят там, в Средней Азии
issues.translation_quote: inside out in Central Asia
issues.justification: Garbled phrase; see above.

issues.source_quote: Может козла забьем? Потом.
issues.translation_quote: Fancy a game of dominoes? Later.
issues.justification: 'Забить козла' is a specific Russian dominoes slang; 'Fancy a game' is a British register mismatch but meaning preserved. Minor.
